conceptZh: 螃蟹有兩隻大鉗子，橫著走
object: a bouncy astronaut toy in a fishbowl helmet and a little red crab
morph: the astronaut builds a wrong space-rocket shape first, then rebuilds it into 蟹
creativeAngle: 太空人玩偶先拼出火箭、再發現不對，改成螃蟹拼出字。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 蟹 (crab). Lead: a bouncy white astronaut toy with a round fishbowl helmet who floats up off the ground whenever he jumps. Moment 1 (0-1.6s): he proudly stacks red stroke parts into a pointed rocket and zooms upward, helmet bumping a ceiling-high cloud as the voice says 蟹. Moment 2 (1.6-3.3s): he notices the rocket is wrong, shrugs, floats down and swaps the pieces with a fast shuffle; at the second 蟹 the parts click into 蟹. Moment 3 (3.3-5s): a small round red crab scuttles sideways across the sand floor to the glyph, claws raised; the voice says 螃蟹 as the astronaut floats up and nose-to-claw with it, the crab pinches his antenna with a harmless boing. Moment 4 (5-8s): glyph still; the astronaut bobs gently while the crab dances sideways. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "蟹、蟹、螃蟹" (ㄒㄧㄝˋ、ㄒㄧㄝˋ、ㄆㄤˊ ㄒㄧㄝˋ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stops; no other speech, no music louder than the voice. The only on-screen text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 蟹, drawn as saturated solid coral red strokes on a pale sky blue background, correctly formed, centered, filling about 70% of frame height with margins, perfectly still for the final 3-second hold while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. No vocabulary text, subtitles, watermark, clutter, flashing, real people or realistic humans; bright but not neon, no dark grading.

conceptZh: 積木小隊正要把最後一塊鉗子積木裝到自己拼的小螃蟹上，調皮小老鼠一把搶走鉗子繞著畫面狂奔，小隊排成一列追著跑、轉彎打滑整排倒下、再疊成高塔飛撲趴地，摔散的積木和打滑痕跡剛好排成蟹字，剩下的積木重新拼成小螃蟹橫著走，老鼠乖乖把鉗子還回來。
object: a squad of red interlocking building bricks with tiny faces, led by a bossy captain brick, chasing a cheeky grey cartoon mouse who stole the pincer brick of their little brick crab
morph: the squad topples at a skidded corner, re-stacks into a tower, takes a flying leap and belly-flops; the scattered bricks and skid trails settle as the strokes of 蟹, with the belly-flop pile forming 虫 at the bottom and the flung pieces forming 角, 刀 and 牛 on top
creativeAngle: 改用追逐模式與積木小隊主角：老鼠搶走蟹鉗引發一整段追逐，小隊「排隊、打滑倒塌、疊塔飛撲」的連鎖肢體笑料把積木摔成蟹字；與前版太空人靜態拼字完全不同，而且「螃蟹」一詞由小隊自己的積木重新拼成小螃蟹橫走來演出，聲音與畫面同一個故事。
promptEn:
An 8-second animated clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 蟹 (crab). Flat pale butter-yellow floor and wall, soft even light, nothing in the background. Lead: a squad of six glossy red interlocking building bricks, each with a tiny face, marching in a tidy column behind a bossy captain brick wearing a stud as a hat. Supporting character: an original tiny grey cartoon mouse with big round ears, lightning fast, always grinning.

Moment 1 (0-1.5s): the squad proudly carries the last piece, a red pincer brick, toward a small crab they built from bricks in the bottom-left corner. The mouse zips in from the right, snatches the pincer brick, and skids to a stop center frame, waggling it with a grin. The captain points, the whole column leans forward and winds up. The voice says 蟹 as they point.

Moment 2 (1.5-3.3s): the chase. The mouse zigzags in a wide loop around the frame; the squad marches after it in a column, legs blurring. At the first corner the column skids, accordions, and topples brick by brick with a clatter, the captain landing upside down. The bricks pop up, snap back together, and run again, bigger loop, closer to camera.

Moment 3 (3.3-4.8s): the mouse darts toward the camera; the squad stacks itself into a single tall tower mid-run, takes a flying leap, hangs in the air for a frozen beat, then belly-flops SPLAT onto the floor with big cartoon squash. The impact flings the bricks apart: the long red skid trails and the flung pieces land on the top half as the parts 角, 刀 and 牛, and the flattened pile beneath settles as 虫. Everything locks into the correctly formed glyph 蟹 as the voice says 蟹 the second time.

Moment 4 (4.8-8s): the glyph stays perfectly still, centered, filling about 70% of frame height with margins. In the bottom-right corner, three leftover bricks reassemble into the little brick crab, which scuttles sideways on tiptoe, clicking its one claw; the voice says 螃蟹 as it scuttles into view. The mouse, caught under the captain's belly, wriggles free, sheepishly hands the pincer brick back, and the crab snaps it on with a happy click. The dizzy captain grins and does a tiny wobbly victory pose, never touching the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "蟹、蟹、螃蟹" (ㄒㄧㄝˋ、ㄒㄧㄝˋ、ㄆㄤˊ ㄒㄧㄝˋ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between each, then stops; no other speech, no music louder than the voice, only soft toy clatters and a gentle splat.

The only on-screen text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 蟹 in saturated solid tomato-red strokes on the pale butter-yellow background, correctly formed and uncropped, still for the final 3-second hold. No vocabulary text, subtitles, watermark, clutter, flashing, real people or realistic humans; bright but not neon, no dark grading.
